title: SLO-driven runtime contracts and rollback playbook
author: Maya R. Thompson
content:
Summary
This document defines a practice for tying public service/API contract changes to SLO-driven runtime acceptance gates and an operational rollback playbook. It standardizes how we declare the runtime impact of API/model/runtime changes, what telemetry must be collected, automated gate thresholds, and the exact steps engineers must follow to roll back or mitigate when gates fail.

Scope
- Applies to changes that alter runtime behavior or the request/response contract for Redwood-hosted inference endpoints and to configuration changes in Dedicated and Private runtime sidecars.
- Includes: new streaming semantics, structured response version bumps, batch/quantization profile switches, kernel scheduling changes, fallback routing, and autoscaling policy changes.
- Excludes purely UI-only changes and documentation-only edits.

Motivation
Making rollout decisions based on signal close to the customer experience reduces blast radius. Historically we relied on ad-hoc dashboards and team conventions; this playbook enforces:
- a single source of truth for contract impact metadata declared during PRs;
- automated SLO gates enforced in CI/CD and at canary runtime;
- a repeatable, fast rollback path with clear ownership.

Definitions
- Contract change class (CC): small | compatible | incompatible | runtime-affecting. Each change must be labeled in the PR.
- Runtime acceptance gate: an automated check that evaluates production-canary telemetry against SLOs for a change window.
- Canary window: default 15 minutes for high-risk changes, 60 minutes for low-risk changes (configurable per change).
- Primary SLOs: availability (p99 success rate), latency (p99), error budget burn.

Contract change classification guide (short)
1. small: internal refactor or non-semantic change with no client-visible effect. Minimal telemetry required.
2. compatible: adds optional fields or expands schema in a backwards-compatible way. Requires structured-response schema validation and unit tests plus canary gate.
3. incompatible: removes fields or changes semantics. Requires staged rollout, documented migration plan, and manual approvals.
4. runtime-affecting: changes that alter batching, scheduling, quantization, kernel selection, or fallback routing. Requires per-case perf tests, a canary in production with robust telemetry, and an automatic rollback policy.

SLO mapping (examples)
- Availability SLO: 99.95% successful responses per region over rolling 30d (primary KPI for breaking changes).
- Latency SLOs: small-req p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 220ms (token generation requests <= 64 tokens).
- Error-rate threshold: client-visible errors < 0.1% over the canary window.
- Quality/regression SLO: measured by eval-set pass-rate; regression alert if drop > 2.5 absolute pts for any critical eval.

Telemetry and instrumentation requirements (must be present for runtime-affecting and incompatible changes)
- Request-id propagation across edge -> router -> runtime -> cache -> model.
- Telemetry fields: request_class (short|long|embedding|batch), model_variant, kernel-path, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, bytes_in, bytes_out, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, trace_id, latency_ms (broken down by stage).
- Structured-response validation failures must be returned as a typed error with error_code = "struct_schema_violation" and increment counter telemetry.http.response_schema_failures.
- Synthetic canary traffic must be generated with both short and worst-case long-context prompts.

CI/CD gates and automation
- PR checklist must include: change classification, required telemetry list, expected SLO impact, rollout plan, automated test matrix (unit, integration, perf), and owner oncall.
- Merge is blocked until: required telemetry is present in canary manifests; perf harness passes; and at least one reviewer with "runtime" scope approves.
- Canary job (pipeline): deploy to canary routing (1-2% traffic), run synthetic tests, evaluate runtime acceptance gate.
- Runtime acceptance gate thresholds are codified in a YAML policy attached to the PR (example below). A failing gate triggers automatic rollback.

Example gate policy (yaml)
---
gate_name: "quantization-profile-switch-2026-11"
canary_window_minutes: 15
thresholds:
  - metric: "p99_latency_ms"
    comparator: "<=\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\"\">= 220"
  - metric: "error_rate_pct"
    comparator: "<= 0.1"
  - metric: "eval_regression_pts"
    comparator: "<= 2.5"
actions_on_fail:
  - "automated-rollback"
  - "notify-oncall-channel"
  - "open-incident-draft"
notes: "Gate evaluates per-region and will fail if any region fails. The canary job gathers per-region metrics and evaluates the policy."

(See appendix for a syntactically valid CI policy template.)

Automated rollback behavior
- Trigger conditions: gate failure, loss of telemetry telemetry pipeline, or manual abort by oncall.
- Rollback steps (automated):
  1) Set routing weight: new_variant -> 0% via router-api (atomic).
  2) Promote previous stable snapshot as active variant.
  3) If the change updated kernel payloads or node-level packages, trigger node drain + redeploy to recover consistent runtime.
  4) Emit structured incident draft (title: "Automated rollback: <change-id>") with initial diagnostics.
- Rollback CLI (example):
  rwinfctl rollout abort --change-id=CHG-2026-1123 --reason="slo_gate_failure"
  rwinfctl rollout promote --variant previous-stable --instant=true
- Manual mitigation when automated rollback is inappropriate: follow the mitigation checklist in the "Mitigation" section below.

Mitigation checklist (when partial rollback or hotfix is preferred)
- Immediately route 100% of traffic to regional fallbacks (fallback-model:safe-1) using the router control plane.
- Throttle ingress (edge) for aggressive error storms: set global edge concurrency cap to 10k requests/min and backpressure hints to clients.
- Push a small configuration patch: e.g., reduce batch size, disable adaptive-kv-prefetch, or lower max_tokens. Test in canary then promote.
- If quality regressions present, revert model artifact and run evaluation suite on the previous weights; escalate to model steward.

Oncall playbook (summary)
1. Acknowledge incident/alert and read automated incident draft.
2. Verify telemetry (sums, p99, error rate) across regions using the pre-made dashboard: "Runtime Gate — Active Canary".
3. If automated rollback triggered: validate rollback completed and monitor metrics for 30m.
4. If no automatic rollback: decide immediate rollback vs mitigation using the guidance above.
5. Post-action: create postmortem ticket and tag the change PR/ADR for follow-up.

Ownership and SLAs
- Change owner: person who authored the PR is accountable until change is stable for 72h.
- Runtime oncall: responsible for executing rollback and triage during the canary window.
- Model steward: accountable for accuracy regressions and for approving re-rollouts after a failed canary.
- SLA to customers: incidents that result in lost availability beyond the SLO must be escalated to customer-success for affected tenants within 4h.

Testing and validation matrix
- Unit tests: required for all changes.
- Integration tests: required when request/response schema changes.
- Perf tests: required for runtime-affecting changes; include 3 synthetic scenarios: best-case (short prompt), worst-case (long prompt), and mixed-batch (80% short, 20% long).
- Chaos tests: optional but recommended for multi-node kernel or eviction algorithm changes.

Post-rollback analysis and prevention
- Postmortem must include: root cause analysis, why gate failed to catch the issue (if applicable), improvements to telemetry or gate thresholds, and a regression test to prevent recurrence.
- If the change misclassified the contract (e.g., runtime-affecting classified as small), add an ADR documenting the revised classification rule.

Appendix A — CI policy template (minimal)
---
canary_targets: [us-west-2, eu-central-1]
traffic_percentage: 1
synthetic_tests: [short-prompt, long-prompt, batch-mix]
metrics_to_collect: [p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, eval_regression_pts]
acceptance_policy: ./policies/<change-id>-gate.yaml
rollback_behavior: automated | manual
owner_oncall: "#eng-runtime-oncall"
notes: "This file should be created and attached to the PR under .ci/canary-policy.yaml"

Appendix B — Example telemetry query (PromQL-like pseudocode)
- p99 latency per region: quantile_over_time(0.99, latency_ms{env=\"prod\",region=~\".*\"}[15m])
- error rate: increase(http_response_errors_total{env=\"prod\",change_id=\"CHG-2026-1123\"}[15m]) / increase(http_responses_total{env=\"prod\",change_id=\"CHG-2026-1123\"}[15m]) * 100

Appendix C — Quick checklist for PR authors
- Label PR with one of: small | compatible | incompatible | runtime-affecting.
- Attach canary gate YAML to .ci/canary-policy.yaml.
- Confirm telemetry fields are emitted and tagged with change_id.
- Add owner_oncall and expected canary window in PR description.
- Schedule a post-merge watch party: 72h for runtime-affecting, 24h for incompatible changes.
